scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Red, yellow, green. Some signals change on a timer, but some seem to know you're waiting. How?

scenes.name: controller
scenes.text: Each junction has a controller box nearby, a small computer that runs the light sequence.

scenes.name: fixed
scenes.text: Simple signals use fixed timing. Each direction gets green for a set number of seconds, based on usual traffic.

scenes.name: sensors
scenes.text: Smarter ones use sensors, like loops of wire under the road, or cameras, to detect waiting vehicles.

scenes.name: adaptive
scenes.text: Then the controller extends green for busy roads, and skips empty directions.

scenes.name: wave
scenes.text: Signals along a road can be linked, so cars at the right speed hit green after green.

scenes.name: safety
scenes.text: Yellow and an all red pause give time to clear the junction before others go.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Timed, sensed, connected. Follow for more on how things really work.
